subject: Slate repack & rollback playbook — approval for tier repack
messages:
From: Maya Chen <maya@luminohealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Dupree <alex.dupree@luminohealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Packaging request: repack to 'Slate' for pilot + downgrade safeguards

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers look great. We have an internal ask from product: they want to pilot the higher-throughput Slate tier for a 30-day pilot on one service, but want two cost-saving levers during the pilot so we can justify the spend to finance:

- Carve out the transcription feature (keep core generation + chat) so we’re not paying full feature set pricing
- A documented rollback/playbook in case quality regressions appear after the pilot

Three specific asks from Lumino:
1) Can Redwood provide a short playbook that defines canary rollout, observable metrics, and an automated fallback to our original tier?
2) If we downgrade within 60 days, can we get a stepdown credit or proration to mitigate the pilot spend?
3) We’ll need a one-page amendment for procurement to sign — procurement prefers a DocuSign link.

I attached a usage snapshot and a proposed scope for the pilot to help you size the canary.

Thanks — would love a quick call tomorrow to align.

Best,
Maya Chen
Director, Product — Lumino Health
[Attachment: current-usage-snapshot.csv (csv)]
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Maya Chen <maya@luminohealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-04T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging request: repack to 'Slate' for pilot + downgrade safeguards

Hi Maya — really appreciate the clear asks. Quick notes and a proposed approach below.

Summary of what we can do immediately:
- Feature carve-out: we can gate the transcription model at the routing layer so you’re billed for Slate compute only on requests that actually need transcription. That reduces effective unit cost without a full SKU change.
- Rollback/playbook: we’ll draft a one-page playbook that includes: canary window (24–72h), key metrics (token success rate, 95th p95 latency, hallucination-rate proxy via rerank score), and an automated fallback policy to the prior tier with a configurable threshold.
- Credits/proration: sales can offer a stepdown credit if a downgrade happens within the first 60 days; propose a 15% onboarding credit applied to pilot consumption and a graduated stepdown credit (15% first 30 days, 7.5% next 30). If that works, we’ll include language in the amendment.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I’ll circulate the draft rollback playbook and a short amendment for procurement by EOD tomorrow.
2) Kimberly, Karthik — can you confirm the legal/finance-friendly phrasing for the stepdown credit and the SLA escape clause?
3) Maya & Alex — share the procurement contact and preferred DocuSign workflow.

I’ve attached a short Slate repack summary and a draft playbook for your review. Happy to hop on a 20-min call to finalize.

Cheers,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: slate_repack_summary.pdf (pdf)]
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-05T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Packaging request: repack to 'Slate' for pilot + downgrade safeguards

Sergio / Karthik — quick internal note (forwarding Sergio’s reply inline).

On Fri, Jun 4, 2027 at 11:03 AM Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Maya — really appreciate the clear asks. Quick notes and a proposed approach below.
> ...

Our position for approvals:
- Credit: agree to the 15% onboarding credit applied as an invoice-level credit for the pilot. For the stepdown credit, legal prefers fixed percentages and a single true-up within 60 days. The proposed 15%/7.5% ladder is acceptable if finance can reconcile on consumption records.
- SLA/escape clause: we must ensure the fallback (automated tier swap) doesn’t create a state where logs/kvs are lost — include explicit language that data retention and KV-cache consistency will be preserved during the automated fallback.
- Amendment/DocuSign: sales can ship the amendment with two optional clauses (a) stepdown credit; (b) rollback SLA escape — procurement picks one. If they pick both, ask Legal to run a quick 2-day review.

Action for Karthik: please draft the short amendment clause for credits + rollback SLA language so Sergio can attach it to the DocuSign packet. Keep it <300 words.

Kimberly Park
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: amendment-draft.docx (docx)]
From: Maya Chen <maya@luminohealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Dupree <alex.dupree@luminohealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@luminohealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-06T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging request: repack to 'Slate' for pilot + downgrade safeguards

Thanks — this is helpful. Procurement (procurement@luminohealth.com) will own the DocuSign flow. We prefer the stepdown credit option but will confirm which clause we want (credit vs rollback SLA) by EOD Monday.

Two logistical notes:
- Can we get the playbook as a markdown file so our SREs can drop it into our runbooks? (md preferred)
- Timeline: we’d like the pilot to start the week of 6/14 if all signoffs complete.

I’ll look for the DocuSign packet and the md playbook.

Best,
Maya
Director, Product — Lumino Health
